ui_bugs.issue: Runtime crash 'destroy is not a function' — useEffect(load, deps) received a function that returns a Promise, so React tried to invoke the returned Promise as a cleanup. FIXED by wrapping as useEffect(() => { load(); }, deps).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py (894 lines) is close to the 700-line guideline threshold — consider splitting into routers (auth, users, certs, spm, misc) for maintainability.
spm_dashboard calls list_reports() twice per request (once for month, once for whole year) — small perf hit; acceptable at current scale but cacheable.
employee_stats issues one Mongo query per staff member (N+1). For 12 users it is fine, but at scale prefer a single aggregation.

download_certificate accepts ?auth=<token> but does not decode/validate the JWT — any non-empty string in the header/query is accepted (only the DB lookup is done through get_object). Consider calling get_current_user for consistency and access control by role.
put_object/get_object are synchronous requests.* calls inside async endpoints and will block the event loop under load — consider httpx.AsyncClient.
Auth is exempt from CSRF but CORS allow_origins='*' with allow_credentials=True is invalid per CORS spec (browsers reject). If cookies are ever added, set explicit origins.

The frontend previously had a class of bugs where useEffect(load, deps) was passing an async function directly (returning a Promise) causing 'destroy is not a function' crashes; this was fixed in 6 pages. If new pages are added, ensure useEffect callback is wrapped: useEffect(() => { load(); }, deps).
rca of the issue: Root cause of the frontend 'destroy is not a function' runtime error: `useEffect(load, [...])` where `load = () => api.get(...).then(...)` returned a Promise. React treats any non-function return value from useEffect as a bug and, on re-render/unmount, tries to call the returned value as a cleanup destroy(). Since a Promise is not a function, it throws. Mitigation applied: wrap in an arrow function `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [...])` so the effect returns undefined.
